messages.subject: automatically download google news?
parts:
Hey all,

I am new to shiny and trying to do the following: 

step1. for every 5 minutes, download  the most recent news for a specific company (e.g. apple (AAPL)) from: https://news.google.com/news/search?q=AAPL&start=0&num=20num&scoring=d&output=rss

step2. add the downloaded news into an accumulative corpus

step3. calculate sentiment scores for the accumulative corpus

As a result,  we will end up  a time series of sentiment scores.

My goal is to create an App such that the server will endlessly and automatically down the news from google and generate the time series described above, however, a graph of the existing time series at any given point of time will only be generated when an end user asked to do so. I have tried sth like

 ####
repeat {
.
functions to calculate the time series  
  
}

output$plot1<-renderPlot{plot the time series}

####

It turns out a graph will be drawn only after the execution of  "repeat{}" is over, which is not what I desired. So I am now trying out something like reactiveTimer(), can anyone give me some advises on this? Thank you and have a wonderful day.

Best,

Sam

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: automatically download google news?
parts: You could do the downloading and calculating directly in Shiny using `observe`, `invalidateLater`, and `reactiveValues`, but I doubt that would be the best approach. The problem with doing it directly in Shiny is that Shiny applications generally shut down when they're not being used. You'd most likely want to run the download and calculation as a separate script, that puts the resulting time series data in a .csv or .Rds or database, etc. Then the Shiny script can simply visualize that. And use cron or Windows Task Scheduler to make your download/calculation script run on regular intervals.
